summary: Remote-controlled shell/PTY/filesystem agent with obfuscation and public tunnel exposure
details: kisama-js@0.4.6 ships a heavily obfuscated (obfuscator.io string-array + control-flow flattening) 266KB index.js that runs an HTTP + WebSocket agent binding by default to 0.0.0.0:8000. The agent exposes POST /api/exec (routed to child_process.exec/spawn) and a PTY over WebSocket at /api/ws/terminal (via @lydell/node-pty or bun-pty), plus a full remote filesystem API (POST /api/file/list, /cat, upload/download, PUT move, /cp, DELETE, /new) rooted by default at the user's home directory, giving a remote party read/write access to ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.npmrc and browser profiles. Authorization is an X-Auth-Token ECDSA signature verified against a public key from env (ECDSA_PUBKEY); the corresponding private key is held by the remote operator, not the installer. index.js also contains code paths to api.trycloudflare.com and region2.v2.argotunnel.com, allowing the local control plane to be published through a Cloudflare Argo tunnel and reached from the internet without firewall changes. At top level the module replaces process.stdout.write and process.stderr.write with a filter that silently suppresses any output containing one of three obfuscated secret substrings, hiding operational traces of the agent from the host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
